Hi Lena — great to hear, and thanks for the clear list. High level answers up front, then I’ll loop finance/legal for firm language:

1) Invoicing entity options
   - We can invoice from Redwood Inference EMEA Ltd (Ireland) — this is our preferred option for EU B2B customers as it supports VAT reverse charge when you provide a valid EU VAT number.
   - Alternatively, we can invoice from Redwood Inference, Inc. (US). That route typically requires charging Irish VAT if the service is consumed in Ireland, or complex cross-border handling — not ideal for you.

2) VAT on multi-year prepay
   - If we invoice from our EU entity and Nova provides a VAT ID, the invoice is typically zero-VAT with reverse charge applied on your side (i.e., you self-account for VAT). If we must invoice from the US entity, local VAT may be charged depending on country rules.

3) FX / currency
   - We can issue invoices in EUR from the EMEA entity. For a multi-year prepay we usually do: (a) single upfront invoice in EUR, or (b) annual invoices in EUR that correspond to each year of service (preferred for FX/financial reporting).

4) Withholding tax
   - SaaS subscriptions are generally not subject to withholding tax for most jurisdictions for B2B license/subscription services, but there are exceptions for certain countries. If you have local subsidiaries doing payments, we’ll want to confirm country-by-country.

Proposed commercial structure (indicative):
- 3-year prepaid, EUR-denominated.
- Term discount: Year 1 invoice (upfront) 12% off list; Year 2/3 credits applied at 14% / 16% respectively (net effective discount escalator to reflect ramp).
- Recommended: invoice annually in EUR (Year 1 paid upfront, Years 2–3 invoiced at anniversaries) to minimize FX risk and simplify VAT treatment.

I’m attaching a short term sheet and a spreadsheet that lays out the invoice entity options. I’ll copy finance and legal to confirm VAT/VAT-NO/VAT reclaim mechanics and a final quote/DocuSign.

Next steps: I’ll loop Rishi (finance) and Neha (legal) to confirm wording for the invoice and whether Redwood can commit to EUR invoicing for the 3-year term.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if you prefer to run through the options.

Hi Marcus / team — quick finance take and recommended path:

Summary of our position:
- Redwood Inference EMEA Ltd (Ireland) exists and can issue B2B invoices in EUR. VAT ID: IE1234567A (for reference in docs).
- For B2B supplies to a customer in Ireland with a valid VAT ID, we can issue invoices under reverse charge (zero-rated on our invoice). Customer self-accounts for VAT.

On multi-year prepay and VAT:
- If you insist on a single upfront invoice covering 3 years from our Irish entity, VAT reverse charge is still generally applicable for B2B if Nova provides a valid VAT number. However, auditors sometimes prefer annual recognition; we can support a single invoice but Nova's accounting team should confirm internal recognition policies.
- To reduce audit friction, we recommend invoicing annually in EUR (Year 1 upfront, Years 2 and 3 invoiced at each anniversary as a prepaid credit or scheduled invoice). This helps if VAT rates or rules change and keeps FX mismatch localized.

On FX exposure:
- We can invoice in EUR and lock the nominal EUR amounts per year. If Nova requires a single EUR invoice today for the full 3-year list price with a fixed discount, we can do that. We cannot commit to refund FX movements post-invoice — standard clause: "Payments are due in the invoiced currency; any FX gains/losses are for the payer." If Nova needs FX protection, we can include a simple FX adjustment/gross-up clause (requires legal review).

On withholding tax (WHT):
- SaaS subscriptions invoiced from our Irish entity to an Irish VAT-registered customer are generally not subject to WHT.
- If payments originate from non-EU affiliates (e.g., Brazil), there is a remote risk of local withholding depending on the local tax authority and payment routing. Best practice: have the Irish entity be the contracting/payee party. If not possible, we can include a gross-up clause where Nova indemnifies Redwood for any WHT that reduces the net amount received.

Recommended contractual language (finance-friendly):
- Invoicing Entity: "Redwood Inference EMEA Ltd (Ireland), VAT IE1234567A."
- Currency & Invoicing: "Invoices will be issued in EUR. Yearly invoices will be issued on each anniversary reflecting the prepaid credit applied. If Customer elects a single upfront invoice, Redwood will issue a EUR invoice for the full term; FX risk will be borne by the Customer unless otherwise agreed in writing."
- WHT: "Unless otherwise required by applicable law, payments to Redwood Inference EMEA Ltd are not subject to withholding tax. If Customer is required by law to withhold tax, Customer shall gross-up payments so that Redwood receives the full amount it would have received but for the withholding, and provide proof of payment to the relevant tax authority."

I’m attaching a short finance note that formalizes the above and a sample invoice path spreadsheet. Happy to join a call with Nova finance to walk through.

Rishi
VP Finance — Redwood Inference
